title: Secure a ponytail with a plain hair elastic
instruction: Gather the loose hair into a ponytail and secure it with the plain elastic. Leave it held after both hands let go.
setup: An upright 180 x 156 x 230 mm adult practice head on a 190 mm neck stand and 150 x 150 mm base, with twelve loose 24.5 cm synthetic-hair locks rooted across a 72 mm patch at the back. A separate plain silicone elastic, 30 mm inside diameter, with 3 mm cord thickness, rests on two 6 x 16 x 60 mm wooden rests, 33 mm apart between centres. Both grippers have 40 x 24 x 3 mm finger extensions. Nothing joins the locks together or attaches the band to a hand. Restore the photographed layout.
scoring: 1.0 if at least 11 of the 12 locks pass through the elastic, the elastic is no wider than 5 cm and sits 2.5–16 cm below the head centre, and the ponytail remains held for three seconds after release. 0.5 for at least 9 locks through an elastic at that height; 0.25 for at least 6. Otherwise 0. Detached hair or a broken elastic scores 0. Judge the visible locks, band position and released video with a ruler.
fidelity: Flexible lock bundles and a native elastic surface approximate hair and the band. The surface supplies finger contact; rigid patches supply hair/head contact. A native pinch starts in the central 8 mm and holds only the adjacent elastic already enclosed by the real 24 mm faces and releases on opening, 8 mm slip or estimated 6 N tension. Local pinch contacts are filtered while held. The tension estimate is uncalibrated. Hair can bend, escape or snag; no hair or band pose is prescribed.
scores: Development diagnostics only; no validated full-score demonstration or Dream baseline yet.
context: A useful grooming skill combines gathering loose hair with stretching and releasing an elastic around it.
